## FISH & SEAFOOD RECIPES

### RECIPE: Boiled Sturgeon with Horseradish
- ID: fish-1
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-1
- Name: Boiled Sturgeon with Horseradish (Осетрина отварная с хреном)
- Epoch: 16th-17th century
- Time: 1 hour
- Image: /publicimagesfish/osetr.jpg
- Keywords: boiled sturgeon recipe, sturgeon with horseradish, royal fish, ancient Russian fish dishes

**Description:**
Classic boiled sturgeon according to an ancient Russian recipe. A tender Tsar's dish that pairs perfectly with pungent grated horseradish.

**Ingredients:**
- Sturgeon - 1 kg
- Onion - 2 pcs
- Carrot - 1 pc
- Parsley root - 1 pc
- Bay leaf - 2 pcs
- Peppercorns - 5 pcs
- Salt - to taste
- Grated horseradish - for serving
- Vinegar (3%) - 2 tbsp

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Clean sturgeon, remove the notochord (viziga)
2. Cut into serving pieces
3. Place vegetables and spices in a pot
4. Cover with water, bring to a boil
5. Add fish, cook for 20-25 minutes over low heat
6. Remove with a slotted spoon, arrange on a platter
7. Serve with grated horseradish and vinegar

**Historical Context:**
Sturgeon was considered the Tsar's fish. During the reign of Alexei Mikhailovich, there was a special court position of "Master of Sturgeon Affairs." Tsar Alexei Mikhailovich greatly loved sturgeon and demanded it be served at all feasts. Catherine the Great also adored sturgeon, especially with horseradish.

---

### RECIPE: Russian-Style Zander (Sudak)
- ID: fish-2
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-2
- Name: Russian-Style Zander (Судак по-русски)
- Epoch: 18th-19th century
- Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
- Image: /publicimagesfish/sudak.jpg
- Keywords: zander Russian-style recipe, baked zander with pickles, ancient Russian fish recipe

**Description:**
Exquisite zander baked with salted cucumbers, capers, and olives in a rich sauce. A classic of Russian aristocratic cuisine.

**Ingredients:**
- Zander - 1.5 kg
- Salted cucumbers - 3 pcs
- Onion - 2 pcs
- Cucumber brine - 1 cup
- Capers - 50g
- Olives - 100g
- Lemon - 1 pc
- Butter - 100g

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Clean zander, cut into portions
2. Slice cucumbers, sauté them
3. Fry onion until golden
4. Bake fish in the oven for 20 minutes
5. Prepare sauce from brine, capers, and butter
6. Arrange fish on a platter
7. Garnish with cucumbers, olives, lemon
8. Pour sauce over the dish

**Historical Context:**
Zander is one of the most popular fish in Russian cuisine. I.S. Turgenev and A.P. Chekhov mention zander as an exquisite restaurant dish. Nikolai Leskov describes zander as a favorite dish of Russian aristocrats in his works.

---

### RECIPE: Herring Under a Fur Coat (Shuba)
- ID: fish-3
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-3
- Name: Herring Under a Fur Coat (Сельдь под шубой)
- Epoch: Late 19th - early 20th century
- Time: 40 minutes
- Image: /publicimagesfish/seled_pod_shuboy.jpg
- Keywords: herring under a fur coat recipe, classic shuba salad, layered salad with herring

**Description:**
A legendary layered salad with salted herring, vegetables, and mayonnaise. The main symbol of the festive Soviet table and feasts.

**Ingredients:**
- Salted herring - 2 pcs
- Beets - 3 pcs
- Potatoes - 4 pcs
- Carrots - 2 pcs
- Onion - 1 pc
- Eggs - 4 pcs
- Mayonnaise - 300g

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Boil vegetables and eggs, peel them
2. Fillet herring, cut into cubes
3. Grate vegetables separately
4. Finely chop onion
5. Layer: herring, onion, potato, carrot, egg, beet
6. Spread each layer with mayonnaise
7. Decorate as desired
8. Chill for 2 hours before serving

**Historical Context:**
This salad became a symbol of Soviet feasts. Legend says it was created by merchant Anastas Bogomilov in 1918. V.I. Lenin, according to contemporaries, loved simple herring, and the "Shuba" salad became a mandatory dish on the New Year's table during Brezhnev's era.

---

### RECIPE: Rasstegai with Fish
- ID: fish-4
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-4
- Name: Rasstegai with Fish (Расстегаи с рыбой)
- Epoch: 17th-18th century
- Time: 2 hours 30 minutes
- Image: /publicimagesfish/rasstegai_fish.jpg
- Keywords: rasstegai with fish recipe, fish pies, Russian pastry, salmon rasstegai

**Description:**
Traditional Russian rasstegai with a juicy filling of salmon or sturgeon. An open-faced pie that melts in your mouth.

**Ingredients:**
- Flour - 500g
- Milk - 250ml
- Yeast - 10g
- Eggs - 2 pcs
- Butter - 100g
- Sugar - 1 tbsp
- Fish (salmon, sturgeon) - 600g
- Onion - 2 pcs
- Rice - 100g
- Boiled eggs - 2 pcs
- Salt, pepper - to taste

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Prepare yeast dough
2. Let rise for 1 hour
3. Poach fish, flake into pieces
4. Cook rice, chop boiled eggs
5. Sauté onion until golden
6. Mix filling ingredients
7. Roll out dough, cut into circles
8. Place filling, pinch edges leaving an opening on top
9. Brush with egg wash
10. Bake for 25 minutes at 190°C (375°F)

**Historical Context:**
Rasstegai are called so because they are "unbuttoned" (rasstegnuty) on top. Alexander I greatly loved sturgeon rasstegai and ordered them to be served at all receptions. Nicholas II also adored rasstegai, especially with salmon.

---

### RECIPE: Sturgeon Balyk
- ID: fish-5
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-5
- Name: Sturgeon Balyk (Балык осетровый)
- Epoch: 16th-17th century
- Time: 3 days + drying
- Image: /publicimagesfish/balyk.jpg
- Keywords: sturgeon balyk recipe, homemade balyk, dried fish, ancient delicacies

**Description:**
Homemade dried sturgeon or sevruga balyk according to ancient recipes. A Tsar's table delicacy with a rich, concentrated flavor.

**Ingredients:**
- Sturgeon or sevruga - 2 kg
- Coarse salt - 500g
- Sugar - 2 tbsp
- Bay leaf - 3 pcs
- Allspice - 5 pcs

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Fillet fish, remove bones
2. Mix salt, sugar, and spices
3. Rub fish with the mixture on all sides
4. Place in an enamel dish
5. Put under pressure in the refrigerator for 3 days
6. Rinse, soak in water for 2 hours
7. Hang to dry for 5-7 days in a cool place

**Historical Context:**
Balyk (from the Turkic "balyk" - fish) was a delicacy on the Tsar's table. Ivan the Terrible received Astrakhan balyks as tribute. Peter the Great, after visiting Astrakhan, was delighted with the local balyk and ordered it to be supplied to the royal court.

---

### RECIPE: Stuffed Pike
- ID: fish-6
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-6
- Name: Stuffed Pike (Щука фаршированная)
- Epoch: 18th-19th century
- Time: 2 hours
- Image: /publicimagesfish/schuka_farsh.jpg
- Keywords: stuffed pike recipe, whole baked pike, festive fish dish, gefilte fish

**Description:**
A festive stuffed pike, baked whole. A masterpiece of Russian and Jewish cuisine with a tender fish filling.

**Ingredients:**
- Pike - 1.5 kg
- White bread - 100g
- Milk - 100ml
- Onion - 2 pcs
- Eggs - 2 pcs
- Carrot - 1 pc
- Beetroot - 1 pc
- Salt, pepper - to taste

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Clean pike, remove skin like a stocking
2. Separate flesh from bones
3. Grind through a meat grinder with bread and onion
4. Add eggs, salt, pepper
5. Stuff the skin, sew it up with thread
6. Shape like a whole fish
7. Place on a baking sheet with vegetables
8. Bake for 1 hour at 180°C (350°F)
9. Cool, slice into portions

**Historical Context:**
Stuffed pike is a pride of Jewish and Russian cuisine. A.P. Chekhov in the story "Ionych" mentions stuffed pike as a mandatory dish on the festive table. Empress Alexandra Feodorovna, wife of Nicholas II, also loved this dish.

---

### RECIPE: Fish Cutlets
- ID: fish-7
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-7
- Name: Fish Cutlets (Котлеты рыбные)
- Epoch: 19th century
- Time: 1 hour
- Image: /publicimagesfish/kotlety_rybnye.jpg
- Keywords: fish cutlets recipe, homemade fish patties, cod or zander cutlets

**Description:**
Juicy and fluffy homemade fish cutlets made from cod or zander. A classic lean and dietary dish of Russian cuisine.

**Ingredients:**
- Fish fillet (cod, zander) - 600g
- White bread - 100g
- Milk - 50ml
- Onion - 1 pc
- Egg - 1 pc
- Breadcrumbs - 1 cup
- Butter - for frying
- Salt, pepper - to taste

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Soak bread in milk
2. Grind fish through a meat grinder with bread and onion
3. Add egg, salt, pepper
4. Mix the forcemeat well
5. Form into cutlets
6. Coat in breadcrumbs
7. Fry in butter until golden brown
8. Finish in the oven for 5 minutes

**Historical Context:**
Fish cutlets became popular in the 19th century as a lean dish. F.M. Dostoevsky in "The Brothers Karamazov" mentions fish cutlets. In Soviet times, by Stalin's decree, "Fish Thursday" was introduced, when fish cutlets were mandatory in canteens.

---

### RECIPE: Lightly Salted Salmon
- ID: fish-8
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-8
- Name: Lightly Salted Salmon (Сёмга слабосолёная)
- Epoch: 19th century
- Time: 2 days
- Image: /publicimagesfish/semga_sol.jpg
- Keywords: lightly salted salmon recipe, home-cured fish, quick-cured red fish

**Description:**
Perfect home-cured lightly salted salmon. Tender, melt-in-your-mouth fish prepared with dill and lemon.

**Ingredients:**
- Salmon fillet - 1 kg
- Coarse salt - 3 tbsp
- Sugar - 2 tbsp
- Lemon juice - 1 tbsp
- Fresh dill - 1 bunch
- White pepper - to taste

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Rinse fish, pat dry
2. Mix salt, sugar, and pepper
3. Rub fillet with the mixture on all sides
4. Sprinkle with chopped dill
5. Drizzle with lemon juice
6. Place in a container skin-side down
7. Cover with plastic wrap, refrigerate
8. Turn over after 24 hours
9. Ready to eat after another 24 hours

**Historical Context:**
Lightly salted salmon is a traditional appetizer of the Russian North. Pomors have been salting fish since the 16th century. Emperor Alexander III, who loved simple food, particularly appreciated lightly salted salmon and ate it with black bread.

---

### RECIPE: Carp in Sour Cream
- ID: fish-9
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-9
- Name: Carp in Sour Cream (Карп в сметане)
- Epoch: 18th-19th century
- Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
- Image: /publicimagesfish/karp_smetana.jpg
- Keywords: carp in sour cream recipe, baked carp, fish in sour cream, Russian cuisine

**Description:**
Aromatic carp baked in thick sour cream with onion. A hearty and tender dish loved in Russian manor estates.

**Ingredients:**
- Carp - 1.5 kg
- Sour cream - 300g
- Onion - 2 pcs
- Flour - 2 tbsp
- Butter - 50g
- Salt, pepper - to taste
- Fresh herbs - for garnish

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Clean carp, gut it
2. Cut into serving pieces
3. Dredge in flour
4. Fry on both sides until golden
5. Slice onion into rings, sauté
6. Place fish in a baking dish
7. Top with sautéed onion
8. Pour sour cream over everything
9. Bake for 30 minutes at 180°C (350°F)
10. Sprinkle with fresh herbs

**Historical Context:**
Carp was raised in ponds on Russian estates. A.S. Pushkin mentions carp in sour cream as a favorite dish at Mikhailovskoye in his letters. I.A. Goncharov in "Oblomov" describes carp as a festive dish served at name-day celebrations.

---

### RECIPE: Don-Style Ukha (Fish Soup)
- ID: fish-10
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-10
- Name: Don-Style Ukha (Уха донская)
- Epoch: 16th-17th century
- Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
- Image: /publicimagesfish/ukha_donskaya.jpg
- Keywords: Don-style ukha recipe, fish soup with millet and vodka, Cossack fish soup

**Description:**
Rich Don-style ukha made from several types of fish with millet and a shot of vodka. A real Cossack campfire recipe.

**Ingredients:**
- Fish (ruffe, perch, zander) - 1 kg
- Water - 2L
- Potatoes - 3 pcs
- Onion - 1 pc
- Carrot - 1 pc
- Millet - 50g
- Vodka - 50ml
- Bay leaf, peppercorns - to taste
- Fresh dill - for garnish

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Cook small fish for the broth
2. Strain the broth
3. Add potatoes and carrot
4. Cook for 15 minutes
5. Add millet
6. After 10 minutes, add large fish pieces
7. Cook for another 15 minutes
8. Add spices and vodka
9. Let steep for 10 minutes
10. Serve with fresh herbs

**Historical Context:**
Don-style ukha is distinguished by the addition of millet and vodka. Don Cossacks were famous for their ukha, which they cooked over a campfire after fishing. Mikhail Sholokhov in "And Quiet Flows the Don" describes ukha as the main Cossack dish.

---

### RECIPE: Smoked Sprat (Salaka)
- ID: fish-11
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-11
- Name: Smoked Sprat (Салака копчёная)
- Epoch: 19th-20th century
- Time: 2 days + smoking
- Image: /publicimagesfish/salaka.jpg
- Keywords: smoked sprat recipe, home-smoked fish, hot-smoked Baltic herring

**Description:**
Aromatic home-smoked sprat (Baltic herring). A favorite appetizer of St. Petersburg residents and a Baltic classic.

**Ingredients:**
- Sprat (or Baltic herring) - 1 kg
- Salt - 100g
- Sugar - 1 tbsp
- Black pepper - to taste
- Bay leaf - to taste

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Rinse fish, do not gut
2. Mix salt, sugar, and spices
3. Coat fish with the mixture
4. Leave in the refrigerator for 24 hours
5. Rinse, pat dry
6. Cold smoke for 12-24 hours
7. Or hot smoke for 40 minutes at 80°C (175°F)

**Historical Context:**
Sprat is a Baltic herring popular in St. Petersburg and the Baltics. Smoked sprat was a favorite appetizer of St. Petersburg residents. Dmitry Mendeleev, according to contemporaries, loved smoked sprat with his tea.

---

### RECIPE: Fish Pelmeni
- ID: fish-12
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-12
- Name: Fish Pelmeni (Пельмени с рыбой)
- Epoch: 19th century (Siberia)
- Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
- Image: /publicimagesfish/pelmeni_fish.jpg
- Keywords: fish pelmeni recipe, pike pelmeni, Siberian dumplings, lean dumplings

**Description:**
Traditional Siberian pelmeni with a tender fish filling made from pike or zander. A hearty lean dish with a rich history.

**Ingredients:**
- Flour - 500g
- Eggs - 2 pcs
- Water - 200ml
- Salt - to taste
- Fish fillet (pike, zander) - 500g
- Onion - 2 pcs
- Butter - 100g
- Salt, pepper - to taste

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Knead a stiff dough
2. Rest for 30 minutes
3. Grind fish through a meat grinder with onion
4. Add melted butter
5. Roll out dough, cut into circles
6. Place filling, pinch edges
7. Boil in salted water for 5-7 minutes
8. Serve with sour cream or vinegar

**Historical Context:**
Fish pelmeni is a Siberian dish. During Great Lent, they replaced meat pelmeni. Old Believers who moved to Siberia especially loved fish pelmeni. Fyodor Dostoevsky, during his exile in Siberia, tried fish pelmeni and highly praised them.

---

### RECIPE: Dried Vobla (Caspian Roach)
- ID: fish-13
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-13
- Name: Dried Vobla (Вобла вяленая)
- Epoch: 17th-18th century
- Time: 5 days + drying
- Image: /publicimagesfish/vobla.jpg
- Keywords: dried vobla recipe, how to dry fish at home, Astrakhan vobla

**Description:**
Classic dried vobla according to a Volga recipe. The perfect snack, prepared with soul and proper salting.

**Ingredients:**
- Vobla (or bream) - 2 kg
- Coarse salt - 400g
- Sugar - 1 tbsp

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Do not clean or gut the fish
2. Sprinkle salt into the gills and inside
3. Layer in an enamel dish
4. Sprinkle each layer with salt
5. Put under pressure for 5 days
6. Rinse, soak for 3 hours
7. Hang to dry for 7-10 days

**Historical Context:**
Vobla is a symbol of Astrakhan and the Volga River. Dried vobla was the main snack for beer and tea among Volga fishermen. Maxim Gorky, who grew up on the Volga, often mentions vobla as a symbol of Volga life in his works.

---

### RECIPE: Jellied Fish (Zalivnaya)
- ID: fish-14
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-14
- Name: Jellied Fish (Заливная рыба)
- Epoch: 19th century
- Time: 3 hours + setting
- Image: /publicimagesfish/zalivnaya_ryba.jpg
- Keywords: jellied fish recipe, zander aspic, cold appetizer, New Year's jellied fish

**Description:**
Elegant jellied fish (zander or sturgeon) in a clear broth with vegetables. An exquisite cold appetizer for the festive table.

**Ingredients:**
- Fish (zander, sturgeon) - 1 kg
- Gelatin - 20g
- Carrot - 1 pc
- Onion - 1 pc
- Bay leaf - 2 pcs
- Peppercorns - to taste
- Boiled eggs - 2 pcs
- Fresh herbs, lemon - for garnish

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Boil whole fish with spices
2. Strain the broth
3. Add soaked gelatin
4. Break fish into pieces
5. In a mold, layer fish, vegetables, eggs
6. Pour broth over everything
7. Garnish with herbs and lemon
8. Refrigerate until set

**Historical Context:**
Jellied fish is a mandatory dish on the New Year's table. The film "The Irony of Fate" made it iconic. But the recipe existed back in the 19th century. A.P. Chekhov and I.A. Goncharov mention jellied fish as an exquisite appetizer at dinner parties.

### RECIPE: Pomor-Style Cod
- ID: fish-15
- URL: https://russka-kuhnya-9551.vercel.app/recipe/fish-15
- Name: Pomor-Style Cod (Треска по-поморски)
- Epoch: 16th-17th century
- Time: 1 hour
- Image: /publicimagesfish/treska_pomorski.jpg
- Keywords: Pomor-style cod recipe, cod with potatoes and cream, Russian northern cuisine

**Description:**
Hearty cod baked with potatoes and cream according to ancient Pomor recipes. The taste of the real Russian North.

**Ingredients:**
- Cod - 1 kg
- Potatoes - 6 pcs
- Onion - 2 pcs
- Cream - 200ml
- Butter - 100g
- Salt, pepper - to taste
- Fresh dill - for garnish

**Preparation Steps:**
1. Cut cod into portions
2. Boil potatoes, make mashed potatoes
3. Sauté onion until golden
4. Bake fish for 20 minutes at 180°C (350°F)
5. Prepare sauce from cream and butter
6. Place fish on the mashed potatoes
7. Pour sauce over, sprinkle with onion
8. Serve with fresh dill

**Historical Context:**
Pomors in the Russian North prepared cod with potatoes and cream. A simple, hearty dish of northerners who caught cod in the Barents Sea. Mikhail Lomonosov, a native of a Pomor family, fondly remembered cod in his letters.
